lazy_channel_note: Re-measured 2026-08-13, macOS, median of 5 fresh-subprocess samples via import_budget.measure_import_subprocess. The psutil lever this note used to name as 'the next real lever' has been PULLED: coordinator_core/session/core.py no longer imports psutil at module level -- it now lazy-loads it behind an `_UNRESOLVED` sentinel plus a `_psutil()` accessor (see that module's `_psutil`, whose comment cites 2026-08-08-seven-measured-levers-load-norm.md § C1). Confirmed today: `grep -rn '^import psutil\|^from psutil' coordinator_core/` has exactly one hit, a test file (ops/ceremony/tests/test_commit_gate_budget.py), and importing coordinator_core.session.core in isolation pulls 45 modules with psutil absent from sys.modules. Current eager-path figures: coordinator_core.hooks imports 109 modules eager (down slightly from the 2026-08-06 111, elapsed ~23ms). With COORDINATOR_CORE_LAZY_OPS=1 it drops to 24 modules (~8ms) -- much lower than eager, but not the old '5' figure; that OLD number was never re-verified from this session's measurements and should not be quoted going forward. THE LEVER NAMED HERE WAS PULLED, SAME SESSION (2026-08-13). coordinator_core.write_guards.engine had grown from its 2026-08-06 baseline of 69 modules to a measured 142. Root cause: commit 670cf7878 (2026-08-10, C2 unenumerated-agent-type confinement) added a module-level `from coordinator_core.hooks.block_unenumerated_agent_type import resolve_roster` to bash_guards/_helpers.py, which triggered the coordinator_core.hooks package __init__'s full eager registration (18 hooks.* submodules, pulling yaml/subprocess/tempfile) into every write_guards.engine import -- engine.py never imported coordinator_core.hooks directly; it arrived transitively. Fixed by deferring that import behind a lazy module-attribute accessor at all THREE sites carrying the shape (bash_guards/_helpers.py, bash_guards/block_subagent_plan_body_bash_write.py, write_guards/block_subagent_plan_body_write.py), the same pattern session/core.py uses for psutil. Post-fix, re-measured: write_guards.engine 69 (exactly its pre-regression baseline), bash_guards.dispatch 202 -> 159 (back under its 165 ceiling in test_hot_path_hook_import_budget.py), and BOTH now drag zero coordinator_core.hooks.* submodules. The security behaviour of 670cf7878 is unchanged -- import timing only. The pre-existing improvement-queue item (state/improvement-queue/2026-08-06-write-guards-engine-level-import-cost-st-cd99852a6a1f.yaml) flagged eager-discovery cost in principle; this session identified and closed the concrete culprit. NO next lever is named here on evidence: none was measured this session, and inventing a successor would repeat the staleness that made this note misdirect two sessions' engineering decisions.

coordinator_core.write_guards.engine.note: 2026-08-10 REGRESSION, FIXED, not absorbed: commit 670cf7878 (C2, unenumerated-agent-type confinement) added a MODULE-LEVEL `from coordinator_core.hooks.block_unenumerated_agent_type import resolve_roster` to coordinator_core/bash_guards/_helpers.py, which write_guards.engine imports transitively -- that single import dragged in the coordinator_core.hooks package __init__'s full eager registration (18 hooks.* submodules), doubling this entrypoint's cost 69 -> 142 (measured 2026-08-13, prior to fix). A same-day prior dispatch, not yet knowing this was a regression, raised this ceiling to 165 to accommodate the 142 figure -- that accommodation was WRONG (it would have recorded a regression as the new normal) and is reverted by this entry. Fix (2026-08-13, same session): resolve_roster is now imported lazily inside `_helpers.is_confined_by_roster_absence` (and its bash_guards/block_subagent_plan_body_bash_write.py twin site), cached on the module's own `resolve_roster` attribute -- same shape as coordinator_core.session.core._psutil() -- so the existing `monkeypatch.setattr(_helpers, "resolve_roster", ...)` test surface keeps working. Re-measured post-fix (median of 5 fresh-subprocess samples): write_guards.engine is back to the exact 2026-08-06 baseline, 69 modules. Baseline/headroom restored to the pre-regression 2026-08-06 values (headroom 11, ~16% of baseline) rather than kept at the inflated interim numbers. NOTE: coordinator_core.bash_guards.dispatch (no manifest entry here; see test_hot_path_hook_import_budget.py's own hardcoded ceiling for that entrypoint) carried a THIRD site of the same defect shape -- coordinator_core/write_guards/block_subagent_plan_body_write.py's own module-level resolve_roster import, reachable from bash_guards.dispatch via block_subagent_plan_body_bash_write's _resolve_subagent_identity import. That site was ALSO fixed on the same lazy-accessor pattern (2026-08-13, same session, EM-inline), closing the last eager pull: bash_guards.dispatch measured 202 -> 159 modules, back under its 165 ceiling, and write_guards.engine / bash_guards.dispatch now drag ZERO coordinator_core.hooks.* submodules. All three sites are lazy; a fourth module-level `from coordinator_core.hooks.block_unenumerated_agent_type import resolve_roster` anywhere reachable from these entrypoints re-opens this regression.
